## `client.artifacts`

Versioned files and directories, stored in the catalog next to tables.

### `client.artifacts.upload`

Signature: `client.artifacts.upload(environment: str, qualified_name: str, path: str | os.PathLike[str], *, sources: Mapping[str, int | None] | None = None, break_glass_reason: str | None = None, limits: ScanLimits | None = None, dir_fd: int | None = None) -> ArtifactVersion`

Store a local file or directory as the next version of an artifact.

The artifact is created on first use. Only files the store does not have yet are sent, so a second version that changes one file sends one file. Version numbers are never reused and can have gaps: do not assume the result is the previous number plus one.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined ``"namespace.name"``. |
| `path` | `str | os.PathLike[str]` | required | A regular file (a single-file artifact) or a directory. Symbolic links, devices, sockets and pipes are refused. Everything in a directory is stored, including hidden files such as ``.env``: point it at a directory that holds only the artifact. |
| `sources` | `Mapping[str, int | None] | None` | `None` | What the version was made from, for lineage: a table, view or artifact name mapped to the artifact version read, or `None` for the current one. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Write to a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. |
| `limits` | `ScanLimits | None` | `None` | What the local scan may look at before it gives up. `None` (the default) uses the limits the server's operator set, read once per client from the info route (the defaults when the server sends none). |
| `dir_fd` | `int | None` | `None` | An open descriptor of a directory: `path` is then ``.`` (that directory) or the name of one file or directory in it, and nothing is looked up relative to the working directory, so a thread that changes it during the upload cannot redirect what is stored. You keep the descriptor open until the call returns and close it yourself. Linux and macOS only. |

Returns: `ArtifactVersion`. The new version, with `files_sent` and `files_reused` set.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the name is not dotted, the tree cannot be stored (`ManifestError`, naming the path), a file changed while it was uploaded, or the server refuses the manifest. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If the caller may not write the name. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the namespace does not exist. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If the upload kept getting lost, or the artifact has too many open uploads. An upload the server refused to commit is withdrawn before the error is raised. |
| `lakana.LakanaConnectionError` | If the server could not be reached, or the answer to the commit stayed lost after every attempt (the version may exist; the message says how to find out). |
| `lakana.InvalidResponse` | If the server's answer is not what a Lakana server sends. |
| `ValueError` | If `dir_fd` is given with a path that is not ``.`` or one name, or on a platform that cannot open files relative to a directory. |

### `client.artifacts.abort_upload`

Signature: `client.artifacts.abort_upload(environment: str, qualified_name: str, upload_id: str) -> None`

Withdraw an upload that was begun and will not be finished.

`upload` does this by itself when it gives up after a failure, or when the server refused its commit; call it for an upload you started some other way, or one a killed process left behind (`list_uploads` shows its id). Only the principal that began the upload can withdraw it, and only while it is open. A task attempt can withdraw only the uploads begun under its own claim, and a superseded attempt still can: withdrawing writes nothing, so it is not guarded, by design. Files it already stored stay on the server until its periodic clean-up finds that nothing names them.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined ``"namespace.name"``. |
| `upload_id` | `str` | required | The upload's id, as the server gave it when the upload began. |

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the name is not dotted, or the id is not an upload id. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not write the name. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no artifact has this name. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If the upload does not exist, is not yours, has expired or was committed. |

### `client.artifacts.list_uploads`

Signature: `client.artifacts.list_uploads(environment: str, qualified_name: str | None = None, *, limit: int = 100, cursor: str | None = None) -> ArtifactUploadPage`

List your own open uploads, newest first, one page at a time.

An upload that was begun and never finished, for example after a killed process, holds one of its artifact's 16 upload places until it expires (one hour by default). Withdraw one with `abort_upload`. Only uploads you began are listed (a task attempt sees its own), never another principal's, and an upload in an artifact you may no longer write is left out. The list does not say how many files an upload has sent.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str | None` | `None` | Only this artifact, dot-joined ``"namespace.name"``; every artifact when `None`. |
| `limit` | `int` | `100` | Uploads per page, 1 to 500; the server refuses a value outside that with a 422. |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`, to fetch the page after it. Pass the same `qualified_name` with every page; `iter_uploads` does this for you. |

Returns: `ArtifactUploadPage`. Up to `limit` uploads, each with `upload_id`, `artifact`, `created_at` and `expires_at`, and the cursor of the next page.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `qualified_name` is not ``namespace.name`` or `cursor` is not one the server issued. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not read the environment. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist. |
| `lakana.InvalidResponse` | If the server's answer is not what a Lakana server sends. |

Signature: `client.artifacts.iter_uploads(environment: str, qualified_name: str | None = None, *, page_size: int = 100) -> Iterator[ArtifactUpload]`

| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist. |

### `client.artifacts.delete_version`

Signature: `client.artifacts.delete_version(environment: str, qualified_name: str, version: int, *, break_glass_reason: str | None = None) -> DeletedArtifactVersion`

Delete one version's files. This cannot be undone.

The version stays in the list, marked deleted, with who deleted it and when, and no files; the other versions are untouched, and so is the lineage that names it. A file another version still has is kept. The server removes the bytes before it answers, unless the version is large: it removes up to a budget and its periodic clean-up finishes. Version numbers are never reused.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined ``"namespace.name"``. |
| `version` | `int` | required | The number of the version. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Delete in a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. |

Returns: `DeletedArtifactVersion`. The version, now with `deleted_at` and `deleted_by` and no files (it is an `ArtifactVersion`), and what the delete did to its files: `freed_files` and `freed_bytes` it removed from storage, `kept_files` and `kept_bytes` that stayed, and `kept`, the files that stayed by reason (`other_version` with the version's number if you may read it, `open_upload`, `left_to_sweep`). The counts are `None` from a server that is older than the release that reports them.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `version` is not a positive integer, or the name is not dotted. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not drop the name (a task token never may), or the environment is protected and no break-glass reason was given. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the artifact or the version does not exist. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If the version is already deleted. |
| `lakana.LakanaConnectionError` | If the server did not answer in time; the version may have been deleted (the message says how to find out). If the connection could not be opened at all, the message says nothing was sent. |
| `lakana.ServerError` | If a gateway answered 502, 503 or 504, which says nothing about whether the version was deleted (the message says how to find out), or the server failed otherwise. |
| `lakana.InvalidResponse` | If the server's answer is not what a Lakana server sends. |

### `client.artifacts.drop`

Signature: `client.artifacts.drop(environment: str, qualified_name: str, *, break_glass_reason: str | None = None) -> None`

Drop an artifact: every version, its files and its grants. This cannot be undone.

The name becomes free and a new artifact of that name starts at version 1. The server removes the files inside this request, so for an artifact with thousands of files it can take minutes (the call waits up to ten); if the server fails part-way, its periodic clean-up finishes.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined ``"namespace.name"``. |
| `break_glass_reason` | `str | None` | `None` | Drop in a protected environment outside a run: 10-500 characters, needs `MANAGE_ENVIRONMENT`, audited. |

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the name is not dotted, or belongs to a table or a view. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not drop the name (a task token never may), or the environment is protected and no break-glass reason was given. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If no artifact has this name. |
| `lakana.Conflict` | If a deployed project produces the artifact: remove its asset in git and deploy, then drop it, or delete single versions to free space now. |
| `lakana.LakanaConnectionError` | If the server did not answer in time; the artifact may be dropped (the message says how to find out). If the connection could not be opened at all, the message says nothing was sent. |
| `lakana.ServerError` | If a gateway answered 502, 503 or 504, which says nothing about whether the artifact was dropped (the message says how to find out), or the server failed otherwise. |

### `client.artifacts.download`

Signature: `client.artifacts.download(environment: str, qualified_name: str, directory: str | os.PathLike[str], *, version: int | None = None, read_only: bool = False, dir_fd: int | None = None) -> ArtifactDownload`

Write a version's files into a new or an empty directory on this machine.

The tree appears in `directory` only when every file has arrived and matches its size and SHA-256 in the manifest; a download that fails (a bad manifest, a file that does not match, a connection that breaks, a full disk) leaves nothing at `directory`: a directory that did not exist is not there, one that existed is empty again. An existing empty directory is never replaced: it keeps its place, its mode and whoever stands in it, and the files are moved into it at the end (not as one atomic step: a process killed at that moment leaves some files in it and the rest in a hidden ``.&lt;name&gt;.lakana-partial-*`` directory inside it; empty `directory`, including that hidden one, and download again). Nothing is written through a link.

Permissions: the copy is private to you, as the artifact's contents are access-controlled on the server and a world-readable copy on a shared machine would leak them. Files are 0600 and directories 0700 (less your umask) and nothing is executable. To open a copy to others run ``chmod -R a+rX DIR``. With `read_only` files are 0400 and directories 0500 instead, so that nothing can change them by accident; remove such a copy with ``chmod -R u+w DIR`` first, then ``rm -r DIR``. A `directory` that did not exist is sealed as a whole before it is moved into place, itself included. For an existing empty one, the top-level directories are sealed right after they are moved in, and `directory` keeps its own mode; to have the root sealed too, pass one that does not exist yet.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `qualified_name` | `str` | required | Dot-joined ``"namespace.name"``. |
| `directory` | `str | os.PathLike[str]` | required | Where to write: a new directory (its parents are created), or an empty one. |
| `version` | `int | None` | `None` | The number; the current version when `None`. |
| `read_only` | `bool` | `False` | Make the copy read-only: files 0400 and directories 0500 (the directory itself only if this call created it). The default is private and deletable (0600/0700). |
| `dir_fd` | `int | None` | `None` | An open descriptor of the directory to write in: `directory` is then one new or empty name in it, and the directory is never looked up by path, so the copy lands in the one the descriptor names even if its path has since been moved or replaced by a link. You keep the descriptor open until the call returns and close it yourself. Linux and macOS only. |

Returns: `ArtifactDownload`. `path` is `directory` (resolved) for a directory artifact, and ``&lt;directory&gt;/&lt;file name&gt;`` for a single file. With `dir_fd` it is relative to that directory: ``&lt;directory&gt;`` or ``&lt;directory&gt;/&lt;file name&gt;``.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the artifact or version does not exist, or the version was deleted. |
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not read the name. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If the server's manifest has a path this client refuses, or `directory` is a link, is in use, is too small for the artifact, cannot be created or written to, or the file system refused a write (`ManifestError`: the message names the path and the system's reason). |
| `lakana.ArtifactCorrupt` | If a file does not match the manifest (it may be a transient fault). |
| `StoredManifestDamaged` | An `ArtifactCorrupt`: the manifest does not match its digest, the record is damaged on the server and downloading again cannot help. |
| `StoredManifestInvalid` | A `ValidationError`: the server's manifest breaks a rule this client enforces (a path it refuses, a size out of range); the same on every download. |
| `lakana.LakanaConnectionError` | If the server could not be reached, or the connection ended before a file was complete (the message then says that a server also ends a download slower than 64 KiB/s). |
| `lakana.ServerError` | If the server answered 503 for every one of six tries at a file, over about 30 seconds (busy with other downloads, or unable to serve the file: the message says which, with the server's own text). |
| `lakana.InvalidResponse` | If the server's answer is not what a Lakana server sends. |
| `ValueError` | If `dir_fd` is given with a `directory` that is not one name, or on a platform that cannot write files relative to a directory. |

### `client.artifacts.list`

Signature: `client.artifacts.list(environment: str, namespace: str | None = None, *, limit: int | None = None, cursor: str | None = None) -> builtins.list[Artifact]`

List one page of the artifacts of an environment that you may read.

`list_page` also returns the cursor of the next page, and `iter` walks every page.

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment` | `str` | required | The environment name. |
| `namespace` | `str | None` | `None` | Only this dot-joined namespace path; every namespace when `None`. |
| `limit` | `int | None` | `None` | Most artifacts returned (1 to 200); `None` leaves it to the server (100). |
| `cursor` | `str | None` | `None` | A previous page's `next_cursor`. Send the same `namespace`. |

Returns: `list of Artifact`. Ordered by namespace and name. An artifact you may not read is not listed.

| Error | When |
|---|---|
| `lakana.PermissionDenied` | If you may not read the environment. |
| `lakana.NotFound` | If the environment does not exist. |
| `lakana.ValidationError` | If `cursor` is not one the server issued. |
| `lakana.InvalidResponse` | If the server's answer is not what a Lakana server sends. |
